external_sources.title: Government careers guidance: writing a CV
external_sources.supports: A CV summarises relevant skills, learning and experience. Tailor it to the role, update it and check accuracy. This classroom draft omits private contact and referee details.

external_sources.title: Government careers guidance: application forms
external_sources.supports: Read the form and role requirements; match truthful experience to the questions; review the completed form. School or voluntary experience may be relevant. This is an offline practice form, not a submitted application.

evidence.description: An individual classroom CV draft with role, profile, skills and true examples, learning and experience status; one feedback-led revision, response mode, support and unresolved gaps are recorded.
evidence.status: contribution to source assessment; no completion claim

routes.Supported: Supported: select a real example with staff.
routes.Independent: Independent: draft a short CV using evidence.
routes.Aspire: Aspire: tailor two examples to the role.

vocab.definition: A short record of skills, learning and experience.
Something you can learn to do.
An example that supports a claim.
A job or set of tasks.
Make something clearer or more accurate.

cases.text: The role needs careful sorting. A learner sorted class kit by label.
cases.fact: Sorting by label matches a task in the role.
cases.next_step: Describe the actual action and any support.
cases.staff_note: It is an adult scenario, not evidence that every pupil did this.

cases.text: A draft says: I am amazing at all jobs.
cases.fact: There is no action or example to check.
cases.next_step: Replace it with one true skill and a real action.
cases.staff_note: Do not supply a fictional achievement for the learner.

cases.text: A learner helped set out chairs with a partner.
cases.fact: The task involved working with another person.
cases.next_step: Explain their own part and how they worked together.
cases.staff_note: A class activity can show a skill; label the context honestly.

cases.text: The date of an activity is not known.
cases.next_step: Write to check and ask staff to help find the real record.
cases.staff_note: Do not invent or backdate a work history.

cases.text: An adult wrote the whole draft and the learner has not checked it.
cases.fact: The words may not show the learner’s choice or understanding.
cases.next_step: Read it back and record the learner’s own corrections or response.
cases.staff_note: Scribing is valid support when the learner supplies or confirms the meaning.

cases.text: The draft lists a completed award that is still in progress.
cases.fact: Working towards and achieved mean different things.
cases.next_step: Use an accurate status or mark it for staff checking.
cases.staff_note: Do not infer a qualification, registration or completed award.

CAREERS-LAUNCH-A2-W01 · Week beginning 2 November 2026
I Do: 5 minutes.
Teacher: Model each line aloud and make the reasoning explicit. Check a short CV draft is produced, not just a card-sort. Require a role or goal, a brief profile, at least one relevant skill with an authentic example, and honest learning/experience entries. Preserve the original and the learner’s revision after one specific prompt. A missing history or qualification stays to check. The template is deliberately anonymous and incomplete for real-world submission: private contact/referee details are not collected here. Do not assess neat handwriting as a proxy for a careers skill.

slides.notes:
CAREERS-LAUNCH-A2-W01 · Week beginning 2 November 2026
We Do: 5 minutes.
Teacher: Read the hinge aloud, ask for a choice and a reason. B gives an action linked to teamwork, but it belongs in a learner CV only if true for that learner. A is vague and absolute; C is dishonest. Ask what the learner actually did and what help they used. If they choose A or C, contrast an unsupported claim with a real action and recheck using a different skill.

How can I show what I can do?

Before pupils arrive

Print the practice vacancy, CV sheet, six cards and word mat. Gather existing learner work only where available. Agree a read-aloud, scribed or usual communication-aid route. Use paper or an approved offline editor; no login, public upload or real application is required.
Offer processing time, a quiet start and the usual communication support. Capture each learner’s own work. Read the Staff Answers before teaching.

Hinge and reteach

B gives an action linked to teamwork, but it belongs in a learner CV only if true for that learner. A is vague and absolute; C is dishonest. Ask what the learner actually did and what help they used. If they choose A or C, contrast an unsupported claim with a real action and recheck using a different skill.
Access and practice
Supported: select a real example with staff. Independent: draft a short CV using evidence. Aspire: tailor two examples to the role.

Model one CV line using the labelled adult example. During 12-minute practice, pupils draft their own profile, skill and experience entries; give one NS+ prompt. The six-minute capture completes a learner revision and notes support or gaps. Supported means scaffolded choice or exact scribing, not an adult supplying achievements.

Begin evidence during practice and finish during capture. Accept speech, pointing, drawing, writing or usual AAC. Scribe exact words without supplying the assessed reason. No forced pair work or public performance.
Safe teaching evidence and learner voice
Boundaries

No names of pupils, staff, schools, products or platforms in this pack or classroom practice CV. Use learner ID and role labels. Do not collect addresses, phone numbers, private email, dates of birth or referee details. Do not infer achievements or pressure learners to disclose personal history. Keep real evidence in approved staff storage; record gaps openly.
Assessment and feedback

Check a short CV draft is produced, not just a card-sort. Require a role or goal, a brief profile, at least one relevant skill with an authentic example, and honest learning/experience entries. Preserve the original and the learner’s revision after one specific prompt. A missing history or qualification stays to check. The template is deliberately anonymous and incomplete for real-world submission: private contact/referee details are not collected here. Do not assess neat handwriting as a proxy for a careers skill.

Retain actual work, response mode and support. Use VF · WS · I · NS+ (Yellow Box) · // (self-edit) · ? (read back) · R (responded) · E (evidence in the school’s evidence record). R requires Voice, Audience, an NS+ prompt and the learner’s response in their own colour. Record E only after evidence is banked. Blank forms and adult models are not completed learner evidence.
Lundy moments
Space: calm, accessible participation. Voice: a choice, reason or help request. Audience: the adult listens or reads and replies. Influence: record the support or next-step change made in response.
Offer to the Communication portfolio

Explain a relevant skill, listen to feedback and revise a written or spoken statement. The receiving teacher maps authentic responses to their own portfolio. The receiving teacher maps authentic responses to their own portfolio; no communication criteria are assigned here.

Staff answers and response guide
Build and improve a CV
These are possible responses and task guides, not learner observations. Accept a defensible answer based on the facts or actual work. Record each learner’s reasoning and support.
Card key
Card
Judgement or step
Possible action
A
Relevant example. Sorting by label matches a task in the role.
Describe the actual action and any support.
B
Too vague. There is no action or example to check.
Replace it with one true skill and a real action.
C
Teamwork example. The task involved working with another person.
Explain their own part and how they worked together.
D
Detail to check. A date is missing.
Write to check and ask staff to help find the real record.
E
Ownership not established. The words may not show the learner’s choice or understanding.
Read it back and record the learner’s own corrections or response.
F
Inaccurate claim. Working towards and achieved mean different things.
Use an accurate status or mark it for staff checking.
Model and hinge

Adult example: the role needs careful sorting. Weak claim: I am good at everything. Better: I sorted class kit by its label. I checked each item against the list. I say what I did and what help I used. I check the wording, then keep the new draft.

B gives an action linked to teamwork, but it belongs in a learner CV only if true for that learner. A is vague and absolute; C is dishonest. Ask what the learner actually did and what help they used. If they choose A or C, contrast an unsupported claim with a real action and recheck using a different skill.
Individual evidence key

Check a short CV draft is produced, not just a card-sort. Require a role or goal, a brief profile, at least one relevant skill with an authentic example, and honest learning/experience entries. Preserve the original and the learner’s revision after one specific prompt. A missing history or qualification stays to check. The template is deliberately anonymous and incomplete for real-world submission: private contact/referee details are not collected here. Do not assess neat handwriting as a proxy for a careers skill.
Feedback boundaries and next teaching
Card A: It is an adult scenario, not evidence that every pupil did this.
Card B: Do not supply a fictional achievement for the learner.
Card C: A class activity can show a skill; label the context honestly.
Card D: Do not invent or backdate a work history.
Card E: Scribing is valid support when the learner supplies or confirms the meaning.
Card F: Do not infer a qualification, registration or completed award.
Common misunderstandings

A CV is not a list of perfect claims. Skills can come from real class, home or voluntary tasks. Support does not erase learning, but independence must not be invented. A qualification in progress is not an achieved qualification.
Teaching boundary

No names of pupils, staff, schools, products or platforms in this pack or classroom practice CV. Use learner ID and role labels. Do not collect addresses, phone numbers, private email, dates of birth or referee details. Do not infer achievements or pressure learners to disclose personal history. Keep real evidence in approved staff storage; record gaps openly.
Feedback

If a reason is missing, return to the fact or actual work. Re-model a different example, then keep the learner’s own revision. Use NS+ and the learner response in their own colour before R. E means evidence actually banked. Keep safeguarding records separate.
